# SB-1041 Safety bulletin: airborne dust from blasting

Revision: Rev A  
Plant: P3, line P3-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L2-HT03

Hazard description
- Summary: Blasting operations adjacent to the ring rolling heat treat area have generated airborne dust that migrates into the heat treat zone and associated support areas. Airborne particulate presents an inhalation hazard to personnel, can contaminate heat treat loads, and increases the risk of secondary ignition on oiled or lubricated surfaces.
- Background and mechanism: During abrasive blasting, fine particulates entrained in the exhaust plume can become airborne and travel with facility airflow patterns into adjacent process enclosures. When these particulates settle on heated metal, on tooling, or on lubricated components they can create localized hot spots and combustible deposits. Contamination of parts processed in EQ-P3-L2-HT03 has been observed as surface staining and particulate embeds, which necessitate rework and increases exposure for operators who perform cleaning and inspection tasks.
- Health effects: Inhalation of dust can cause respiratory irritation and, with repeated exposure, contribute to chronic respiratory conditions. Fine particulates can also act as ocular irritants. Workers performing cleaning or inspection where dust is present are at higher risk due to close proximity and potential for resuspension of settled material.
- Rationale for bulletin: Immediate administrative and engineering controls are required to limit migration of blasting dust into the heat treat area, preserve product quality, and reduce personnel exposures. This bulletin clarifies required controls, recordkeeping, and references to existing maintenance and operating procedures.

Affected equipment
- Primary affected equipment: EQ-P3-L2-HT03 (Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3). The lubricant part number for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P3-L2-HT03) is CFW-LUB-159.
- Adjacent operations: Blasting stations feeding into or sharing exhaust or return air with the P3-L2 heat treat area. Support areas where handling, inspection, or temporary storage of heat treat loads occurs.
- Personnel roles affected: Operators assigned to EQ-P3-L2-HT03, blasting operators whose work is performed in the same building zone, maintenance personnel performing furnace or exhaust system work, and quality inspectors who handle parts post-process.

Required controls
- Engineering controls:
  - Containment: Ensure blasting booths and enclosures are fully sealed and maintain designed directional airflow away from heat treat enclosures. Integrity checks of booth seals and doors must be completed before blasting begins.
  - Local exhaust: Verify that local exhaust ventilation on blasting equipment operates to capture airborne particulates at the source. Exhaust discharge paths must be routed to prevent recirculation toward EQ-P3-L2-HT03.
  - Filtration: Install or confirm functioning high-efficiency filtration on ventilation systems serving area air handling where practicable to reduce particulate migration.
  - Housekeeping: Implement frequent controlled cleaning of common walkways and staging areas to prevent accumulation and transfer of settled dust into the heat treat area. Use wet methods or HEPA‑equipped vacuuming to minimize resuspension.
- Administrative controls:
  - Work coordination: Schedule blasting and heat treat loads so that blasting activities do not occur simultaneously with sensitive loading or inspection activities in EQ-P3-L2-HT03 when airflow zones overlap.
  - Access control: Limit access to immediate heat treat area during and after blasting until airborne particulate levels are reduced through ventilation and/or settling. Post clear signage and use physical barriers as needed.
  - PPE: Require respiratory protection and eye protection for personnel who must enter areas with visible airborne dust or who perform cleaning of settled dust. Select PPE per SOP-P3-L2-02 and SOP-P3-L2-03.
  - Lubricant handling: When servicing EQ-P3-L2-HT03, follow handling and storage controls for CFW-LUB-159 to prevent contamination by dust; keep lubricant containers closed and stored in a clean, designated cabinet.
- Operational checks and verification:
  - Pre-shift verification of booth integrity and exhaust operation before commencing blasting or heat treat loading.
  - Airflow smoke testing or equivalent verification after any change to ventilation or enclosure seals to confirm directionality away from EQ-P3-L2-HT03.
  - Visual inspection of furnace chamber exteriors, trolleys, and staging racks for particulate deposits prior to placing parts into EQ-P3-L2-HT03.
- Examples of application:
  - If blasting must occur while parts for heat treat are staged nearby, position blast booths with intake facing away from the heat treat area and place temporary enclosures around staged parts. Use HEPA vacuuming of staging surfaces before transfer to EQ-P3-L2-HT03.
  - For maintenance on EQ-P3-L2-HT03 that requires opening access panels, perform a targeted cleaning of surrounding surfaces using wet wipes or HEPA vacuum and wear respiratory protection until work area clearance is documented.

Records to keep and references
- Required records:
  - Booth and enclosure integrity checks and pre-shift ventilation verifications. Retain checklist entries per site document control practice.
  - Records of any airflow verification testing performed after maintenance or modification to ventilation or enclosures.
  - Cleaning logs for areas adjacent to EQ-P3-L2-HT03 where blasting operations may impact staging or handling surfaces.
  - Incident reports for any contamination events in EQ-P3-L2-HT03 that result in part rework or personnel exposure.
- Document references: Refer to MM-P3-L2-HT03 for maintenance requirements related to EQ-P3-L2-HT03, and to SOP-P3-L2-02 and SOP-P3-L2-03 for operating and PPE procedures applicable to blasting and heat treat area tasks.
- Retention and access: Maintain records in the facility document control system under the P3-L2 folder and make available for review during audits and safety reviews.

Effective date
- Effective date: Rev A

Action required: Implement the above controls immediately, update local work instructions to reflect coordination and containment requirements, and ensure personnel are briefed on required PPE and recordkeeping. Contact the plant safety lead for P3-L2 for clarification or to report nonconformance.
